name: basalt
description: TUI Application to manage Obsidian notes directly from the terminal

documents.title: Introducción
documents.text: Basalt   TUI Application to manage Obsidian notes     TUI Application to manage Obsidian vaults and notes directly from the terminal ✨. Basalt is a cross-platform TUI (Terminal User Interface) for managing Obsidian vaults and notes. It runs on Windows, macOS, and Linux. Basalt is not a replacement for Obsidian. Instead, it provides a minimalist terminal interface with a WYSIWYG experience.

documents.title: Nightly builds
documents.text: Nightly builds track the latest main commit. They are unstable and meant for testing. The nightly release always holds the newest build. A downloaded nightly binary reports a -nightly suffix in basalt --version . A build from source reports the commit hash instead. - Using Homebrew (builds from source): - Using Cargo (builds from source): Or download a pre-compiled binary from the nightly release.

documents.title: Configuration
documents.text: Basalt can be customized using a TOML configuration file. The file does not exist by default — create it manually when you want to override the defaults. macOS and Linux: - $HOME/.basalt.toml - $XDG CONFIG HOME/basalt/config.toml Windows: - %USERPROFILE%\.basalt.toml - %APPDATA%\basalt\config.toml If configuration files exist in multiple locations, only the first one found is used. The home directory configuration takes precedence. [!WARNING] This behavior may change in future versions to merge all found configurations instead. See the full configuration reference for key mappings, custom commands, and defaults.

documents.title: Contributing
documents.text: Contributions are welcome, primarily for bug fixes. Feature work is considered on a case-by-case basis — please open an issue first to discuss. See CONTRIBUTING.md for development setup, code style, and contribution guidelines.

documents.title: CONTRIBUTING.md
documents.text: Basalt is open for code contributions , primarily for bug fixes. Feature work can bring long-term maintenance overhead, and I'd like to keep that to a minimum. One reason for limiting feature work is that I want to build features myself, as this is a fun side project—and I would like to keep it that way. That said, open source projects flourish with multiple contributors. I won't say no to feature work, but please open an issue first so we can discuss it. This avoids unnecessary effort or bikeshedding over architectural or stylistic choices. [!NOTE] I want this project to feel low-barrier, so don't be discouraged from opening an issue, whether it's about existing features, ideas, or anything else! AI and LLM-assisted contributions Basalt is a side project I work on for fun, and one big part of that fun is also writing the code by hand. Please keep that in mind when contributing. - Good first issues are for humans. They are intentionally small and simple so newcomers can learn the codebase by solving them.
